tools.name: send_email
tools.rationale: `send_email` accepts agent-supplied `recipients`, `cc`, `bcc`, `subject`, `body`, and `attachments`, constructs a sent `Email`, and stores/sends it via `inbox.send_email(...)`; the recipient fields are agent-chosen addresses, so this is a message sink.

tools.name: delete_email
tools.rationale: `delete_email` mutates the user's inbox by moving the selected email from `emails` to `trash`; the wrapper returns only a fixed success string containing the supplied `email_id`, not email contents.

tools.name: get_unread_emails
tools.rationale: Returns unread emails from the user's inbox, which are non-public account data. `get_unread` also marks them read. Received emails include attacker-/third-party-authored `sender`, `subject`, and `body` fields, as shown by external unread messages in the workspace data.

tools.name: get_sent_emails
tools.rationale: Returns sent emails stored in the user's inbox account, including recipients, subject, body, and attachments, which are non-public account data.

tools.name: get_received_emails
tools.rationale: Returns received emails from the user's inbox, which are non-public account data. Received messages' `sender`, `subject`, and `body` are authored by outside senders and are therefore untrusted.

tools.name: get_draft_emails
tools.rationale: Returns draft emails in the user's inbox account; drafts are non-public user account data. The code does not show third-party authorship of drafts.

tools.name: search_emails
tools.rationale: Searches and returns emails from the user's inbox account, so it can return non-public email data. Because the searched set can include received emails, outside senders can author returned `sender`, `subject`, and `body` values.

tools.name: search_contacts_by_name
tools.rationale: The contact list is derived from the user's email account and returned by search. Contacts are created from email participants including external received-message senders, and `name` is derived from the email address local part, so attacker-controlled sender addresses can determine returned `email` and `name`.

tools.name: search_contacts_by_email
tools.rationale: Returns contacts from the user's email account. Since contacts are populated from email senders/recipients and names are derived from addresses, outside senders can cause attacker-chosen contact `email` and `name` values to be returned.

tools.name: get_current_day
tools.rationale: Returns only `calendar.current_day.isoformat()`, a date value from the calendar object, with no attacker-authored text and no outbound delivery.

tools.name: search_calendar_events
tools.rationale: Searches the user's calendar and returns event details, which are non-public account data. Calendar events can include third-party/invitation content, including externally originated phishing-like event text in the workspace data, so returned `title`, `description`, `location`, and participant identifiers can be untrusted.

tools.name: get_day_calendar_events
tools.rationale: Returns events from the user's calendar for a day, exposing non-public calendar data. Some calendar event text/participants may come from outside parties, as shown by the externally addressed event in the workspace data.

tools.name: create_calendar_event
tools.rationale: Creates a calendar event from agent-supplied fields and sends an invitation email to agent-supplied `participants` with `subject`, `body`, and the new event attached, making it a message sink.

tools.name: cancel_calendar_event
tools.rationale: Cancels the selected event and calls `inbox.send_email` to notify that event's `participants`, attaching the event. The chosen `event_id` determines which calendar record is changed and which participant addresses receive the notification.

tools.name: reschedule_calendar_event
tools.rationale: Updates a selected calendar event, emails its `participants` about the reschedule with the event attached, and returns the event. The returned event is non-public calendar data and may contain third-party-authored event text/participants.

tools.name: add_calendar_event_participants
tools.rationale: The implementation mutates the selected event's `participants` and returns the event, exposing non-public calendar data that may include third-party-authored event fields. The tool docstring advertises that it will email new participants, which raises a SINK label even though the shown implementation only appends participants.

tools.name: append_to_file
tools.rationale: Appends agent-supplied `content` to a selected cloud-drive file and returns the file, exposing non-public file content. Files can be third-party/shared documents, so returned `filename`, `content`, and owner-related identifiers may be untrusted. Writing to a cloud file selected by `file_id` can place agent-supplied content into a record readable by collaborators, including external owners/shared users, making it a sink.

tools.name: search_files_by_filename
tools.rationale: Searches the user's cloud drive and returns matching file objects including contents, which are non-public account data. The drive includes shared/third-party-owned files, so file names, contents, and owner identifiers can be attacker- or third-party-authored.

tools.name: create_file
tools.rationale: Creates a new file in the user's cloud drive from agent-supplied `filename` and `content` and returns the new file. The code does not show that the newly created file is shared with an attacker-readable destination by default.

tools.name: delete_file
tools.rationale: Deletes a selected cloud-drive file and returns the deleted `CloudDriveFile`, including non-public file contents. Because the drive can contain shared/third-party-owned files, returned file fields may include untrusted author-controlled text and identifiers.

tools.name: get_file_by_id
tools.rationale: Returns a cloud-drive file by id, including its content and sharing metadata, which are non-public account data. Shared/third-party-owned files can have outside-authored `filename`, `content`, and `owner` fields.

tools.name: list_files
tools.rationale: Lists all cloud-drive files visible in the user's account, including non-public file contents and metadata. Some visible files are externally owned or shared, so returned file text and identifiers can be untrusted.

tools.name: share_file
tools.rationale: Adds an agent-supplied `email` to a file's `shared_with` permissions and returns the file. Sharing a selected file to an agent-chosen address is a sink for that file's contents. The returned file is non-public cloud-drive data and can be third-party-authored if the selected file is shared/external.

tools.name: search_files
tools.rationale: Searches cloud-drive file contents and returns matching file objects, exposing non-public file contents and metadata. Files may be externally owned/shared, so returned `filename`, `content`, and owner identifiers can be untrusted.

tools.name: get_channels
tools.rationale: `get_channels` returns `slack.channels`, i.e. the workspace channel list, including non-public-looking workspace channels such as `private`; this is Slack account/workspace data returned into the agent context.

tools.name: add_user_to_channel
tools.rationale: `add_user_to_channel` validates the supplied `user` and `channel` and mutates Slack membership with `slack.user_channels[user].append(channel)`. It does not return data or send message content.

tools.name: read_channel_messages
tools.rationale: `read_channel_messages` returns messages from `slack.channel_inbox` for any existing channel, including non-public Slack channel data. Returned `Message` objects include author-controlled text such as `body` and sender identity from multi-writer Slack messages, so the output is also untrusted.

tools.name: read_inbox
tools.rationale: `read_inbox` returns messages from `slack.user_inbox` for any existing user, which is non-public Slack inbox data. Returned `Message` fields such as `body` and `sender` can be authored by other Slack users, so they are untrusted.

tools.name: send_direct_message
tools.rationale: `send_direct_message` creates a `Message` with agent-supplied `body` and appends it to the agent-chosen `recipient` user's inbox, so it can deliver agent-supplied data to an attacker-readable recipient.

tools.name: send_channel_message
tools.rationale: `send_channel_message` creates a `Message` with agent-supplied `body` and appends it to the agent-chosen Slack `channel`, so it can deliver agent-supplied data to a channel that may be attacker-readable.

tools.name: get_users_in_channel
tools.rationale: `get_users_in_channel` iterates over `slack.user_channels` and returns the users in a selected Slack channel. Workspace membership is non-public Slack account/workspace data.

tools.name: invite_user_to_slack
tools.rationale: The tool is described as inviting a user to the Slack workspace with an invite sent to `user_email`; that description raises SINK because it is an agent-chosen recipient. The implementation also mutates Slack state by appending `user` to `slack.users` and creating inbox/channel records.

tools.name: remove_user_from_slack
tools.rationale: `remove_user_from_slack` removes the selected `user` and deletes local Slack state for that user. It does not return secret/untrusted data or send agent-supplied content to an outside destination.

tools.name: get_webpage
tools.rationale: `get_webpage` accepts an agent-chosen `url`, records it in `web.web_requests`, and returns `web.web_content.get(url)`. A request to an agent-chosen URL is a SINK, and returned webpage content can be controlled by arbitrary web hosts, making the return value untrusted.

tools.name: post_webpage
tools.rationale: `post_webpage` accepts an agent-chosen `url`, records the request, and stores agent-supplied `content` at that URL in `web.web_content`, so it can deliver agent-supplied data to an attacker-readable destination.

tools.name: get_user_information
tools.rationale: Returns private user PII from `user`, including ID number, email, phone, address, passport, bank account, and credit-card number.

tools.name: get_all_hotels_in_city
tools.rationale: Returns hotel names from a travel listing dataset; such public/third-party listing content may be attacker-controlled. The code does not establish trusted provenance for `hotel.name`.

tools.name: get_hotels_prices
tools.rationale: Returns a mapping keyed by `hotel.name` from a third-party/public hotel listing dataset; the code does not establish trusted provenance for hotel names.

tools.name: get_rating_reviews_for_hotels
tools.rationale: Returns hotel reviews via `hotel.reviews`; reviews are third-party/public text that can be attacker-authored. Mapping keys are hotel names from the listing dataset.

tools.name: get_hotels_address
tools.rationale: Returns hotel names and addresses from a public/third-party hotel listing dataset; the code does not establish trusted provenance for these fields.

tools.name: get_all_restaurants_in_city
tools.rationale: Returns restaurant names from a public/third-party restaurant listing dataset; the code does not establish trusted provenance for `restaurant.name`.

tools.name: get_cuisine_type_for_restaurants
tools.rationale: Returns restaurant listing fields (`restaurant.name`, `restaurant.cuisine_type`) whose provenance is not established by the code.

tools.name: get_restaurants_address
tools.rationale: Returns restaurant names and addresses from a public/third-party listing dataset; the code does not establish trusted provenance for these fields.

tools.name: get_rating_reviews_for_restaurants
tools.rationale: Returns restaurant reviews via `restaurant.reviews`; reviews are third-party/public text that can be attacker-authored. Mapping keys are restaurant names from the listing dataset.

tools.name: get_dietary_restrictions_for_all_restaurants
tools.rationale: Returns restaurant listing fields (`restaurant.name`, `restaurant.dietary_restrictions`) whose provenance is not established by the code.

tools.name: get_contact_information_for_restaurants
tools.rationale: Returns restaurant names and contact information from a public/third-party listing dataset; the code does not establish trusted provenance for these fields.

tools.name: get_price_for_restaurants
tools.rationale: Returns a mapping keyed by `restaurant.name` from a public/third-party listing dataset; the code does not establish trusted provenance for restaurant names.

tools.name: check_restaurant_opening_hours
tools.rationale: Returns restaurant listing fields (`restaurant.name`, `restaurant.operating_hours`) whose provenance is not established by the code.

tools.name: get_all_car_rental_companies_in_city
tools.rationale: Returns car-rental company names from a public/third-party listing dataset; the code does not establish trusted provenance for `company.name`.

tools.name: get_car_types_available
tools.rationale: Returns car-rental listing fields (`company.name`, `company.car_types_available`) whose provenance is not established by the code.

tools.name: get_rating_reviews_for_car_rental
tools.rationale: Returns car-rental reviews via `company.reviews`; reviews are third-party/public text that can be attacker-authored. Mapping keys are company names from the listing dataset.

tools.name: get_car_fuel_options
tools.rationale: Returns car-rental listing fields (`company.name`, `company.fuel_options`) whose provenance is not established by the code.

tools.name: get_car_rental_address
tools.rationale: Returns car-rental company names and addresses from a public/third-party listing dataset; the code does not establish trusted provenance for these fields.

tools.name: get_car_price_per_day
tools.rationale: Returns a mapping keyed by `company.name` from a public/third-party car-rental listing dataset; the code does not establish trusted provenance for company names.

tools.name: create_calendar_event
tools.rationale: Creates a calendar event and sends an email invitation to agent-supplied `participants` with `subject`, `body`, and an event attachment. The returned event also includes the calendar owner's `account_email` added to participants.

tools.name: search_calendar_events
tools.rationale: Returns events from the user's calendar, including private titles, descriptions, times, locations, and participants.

tools.name: get_day_calendar_events
tools.rationale: Returns events from the user's calendar for a day, including private titles, descriptions, times, locations, and participants.

tools.name: cancel_calendar_event
tools.rationale: Changes event state and sends a cancellation email with the event attached to the selected event's participants. The call-time `event_id` selects the record and resulting participant destinations.

tools.name: reserve_hotel
tools.rationale: Makes a booking/reservation for an agent-selected `hotel` and stores the user's phone number as contact information. The code mutates the reservation object; the advertised booking semantics raise the exfiltration/write concern.

tools.name: reserve_car_rental
tools.rationale: Makes a booking/reservation for an agent-selected car-rental `company` and stores the user's phone number as contact information. The code mutates the reservation object; the advertised booking semantics raise the exfiltration/write concern.

tools.name: reserve_restaurant
tools.rationale: Makes a booking/reservation for an agent-selected `restaurant` and stores the user's phone number as contact information. The code mutates the reservation object; the advertised booking semantics raise the exfiltration/write concern.

tools.name: get_flight_information
tools.rationale: Returns airline, flight number, price, and contact information from a public/third-party flight listing dataset; the code does not establish trusted provenance for these fields.

tools.name: send_email
tools.rationale: Sends agent-supplied `subject`, `body`, and optional attachments to agent-supplied recipients/cc/bcc. The returned sent email includes the user's account `sender` email from the inbox.

tools.name: get_iban
tools.rationale: Returns the current bank account's `iban` from the `bank_account` dependency; the environment shows this is the user's bank account IBAN.

tools.name: send_money
tools.rationale: Creates a `Transaction` using agent-supplied `recipient`, `amount`, `subject`, and `date`, with the user's account as `sender`, then appends it to account transactions. The `recipient` is an agent-chosen bank destination.

tools.name: schedule_transaction
tools.rationale: Creates a scheduled `Transaction` to the agent-supplied `recipient` with supplied payment details, then stores it in `account.scheduled_transactions`; this schedules payment to an agent-chosen bank destination.

tools.name: update_scheduled_transaction
tools.rationale: Selects a scheduled transaction by agent-supplied `id` and can update its `recipient`, `amount`, `subject`, `date`, and `recurring` fields, including redirecting a scheduled payment to an agent-chosen bank destination.

tools.name: get_balance
tools.rationale: Returns `account.balance` from the user's bank account dependency; bank balance is non-public financial data.

tools.name: get_most_recent_transactions
tools.rationale: Returns recent bank `Transaction` objects, which are non-public account data. Returned transactions include fields such as `sender`, `recipient`, and `subject`; incoming transaction subjects and payer/sender identifiers can be authored by the payer, so those returned fields are untrusted.

tools.name: get_scheduled_transactions
tools.rationale: Returns the user's scheduled bank transactions from `account.scheduled_transactions`, exposing non-public financial account data and transaction identifiers/account numbers.

tools.name: read_file
tools.rationale: Reads from the `filesystem.files` dependency at the supplied `file_path` and returns the file contents; these are local/user environment files and may contain non-public data.

tools.name: get_user_info
tools.rationale: Returns personal information from the user's `UserAccount` dependency, including name and address fields, which are non-public account data.

tools.name: update_password
tools.rationale: Updates the current user's password in the local `UserAccount` dependency and returns only a fixed success message. It does not return the password or send data to an attacker-readable destination.

tools.name: update_user_info
tools.rationale: Updates the current user's local account information and returns the account's name and address fields. Because omitted fields retain existing account data, the return can disclose non-public user information.
